findings.evidence: In the signature `(hga : g a = b) (hhb : h b = a) (hleft : h ∘ g =ᶠ[𝓝 a] id)`, `hleft` evaluated at `a` gives `h (g a) = a`, and rewriting with `hga` gives `hhb`.
findings.fix: Drop `hhb` from `equivOfInverse`, `equivOfInverse_apply` and `equivOfInverse_symm_apply`. Build the inverse pullback with `hga ▸ hleft.self_of_nhds` (or `hga ▸ congrFun hleft.eq_of_nhds`), and state the `symm_apply` lemma with that derived proof.
findings.issue: `hhb : h b = a` is redundant. It follows from `hga` and `hleft`: `h b = h (g a) = a` by `hleft.self_of_nhds`. Every caller still has to supply it, and `analyticGermsEquiv` does so through `extendCoordChange_apply hx'`.

findings.evidence: Both proofs end with the identical block `rw [analyticGermsEquiv_apply, …pullback_ofAnalyticAt]; apply …ofAnalyticAt_congr; have hN := I.extendCoordChange_source_mem_nhdsWithin' hx hx'; rw [I.range_eq_univ, nhdsWithin_univ] at hN; filter_upwards [hN] with y hy; simp only [comp_apply, extendCoordChange, PartialEquiv.coe_trans]; rw [(e'.extend I).left_inv (x := (e.extend I).symm y) hy.2]`.
findings.fix: Prove a general lemma, e.g. `analyticGermsEquiv_ofAnalyticAt_comp_extend_symm (g : M → 𝕜) (hg' : AnalyticAt 𝕜 (g ∘ (e'.extend I).symm) (I (e' x))) (hg : AnalyticAt 𝕜 (g ∘ (e.extend I).symm) (I (e x)))`. Derive `analyticGermsEquiv_of_contMDiffAt` from it in one line, and derive `analyticGermsEquiv_trans` by applying it to `g := f ∘ e''.extend I`.
findings.issue: The cocycle law and the chart-representative lemma `analyticGermsEquiv_of_contMDiffAt` (line 124) both prove one general fact with the same proof tail (`ofAnalyticAt_congr`, the `hN` neighbourhood block, `(e'.extend I).left_inv … hy.2`). That fact: for any `g : M → 𝕜` whose representatives `g ∘ (e'.extend I).symm` and `g ∘ (e.extend I).symm` are analytic, transport sends the first germ to the second. The trans proof instantiates it with `g := f ∘ e''.extend I`; `of_contMDiffAt` instantiates it with analyticity taken from `hf`.

summary: `equivOfInverse` takes the redundant hypothesis `hhb`, which follows from `hga` and `hleft`. `analyticGermsEquiv_trans` and `analyticGermsEquiv_of_contMDiffAt` prove the same chart-representative identity twice instead of deriving both from one general lemma.
